decision_requested: Should Portable Case Pack v1 execute its published Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema as the structural authority before semantic validation?

recommendation.statement: Execute the published Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema first, then run the semantic validator for cross-field domain invariants.

options.action: Use the JSON Schema as structural authority and the semantic validator as the cross-field authority.
benefits: Published required, closed-shape, enum, type, and date-time rules become executable.
Structural and semantic responsibilities are explicit instead of overlapping ambiguously.
risks: Previously tolerated but schema-invalid instances may begin failing and require compatibility review.
options.reversibility: High; CI ordering and validator invocation can be reverted, while compatibility findings remain observable.

options.action: Keep the handwritten semantic validator as the only runtime gate.
benefits: Avoids exposing new schema-validation failures immediately.
risks: Retains a false-ready condition where an instance can contradict the published structural contract and still be accepted.
options.reversibility: High, but the unresolved contract mismatch remains active until changed.

strongest_counterevidence: A closed schema can reveal compatibility failures in previously tolerated instances, so schema execution may create short-term migration work.
unknowns: Whether every derived claim must carry evidence remains outside this decision and requires a separate semantic-contract review.
This public replay does not establish private downstream adoption or business value.
largest_risk: Mistaking structural conformance for semantic correctness; both gates remain required.
latest_safe_decision_time: Before another runtime or downstream consumer relies on Portable Case Pack v1 validation behavior.
minimum_response: A | B | defer until <specific compatibility evidence>
